claims.text: The as-deposited coating is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited coating contains negligible secondary-phase precipitates.
Aging at 600 °C for 10 h induces coherent BCC nanoprecipitates in the FCC matrix.
The induced BCC nanoprecipitates have a volume fraction of approximately 5–10%.
The induced BCC nanoprecipitates have an average diameter of approximately 20–50 nm.
Coherent BCC nanoprecipitates act as strong obstacles to dislocation motion during sustained loading.
Dislocations bow and loop around the coherent BCC nanoprecipitates by an Orowan mechanism.
The nanoprecipitates increase the stress required for steady-state creep.
Orowan strengthening by the BCC nanoprecipitates reduces the steady-state creep rate.
At 600 °C and 200 MPa, the aged coating will have at least a 50% lower steady-state creep rate than the as-deposited coating.
The as-deposited coating has a steady-state creep rate of approximately 1×10^-6 s^-1 at 600 °C and 200 MPa.
The precipitate-strengthening effect is maintained from 550 °C to 650 °C.
The precipitate-strengthening effect is maintained from 150 MPa to 250 MPa.
Above 700 °C, precipitate coarsening reduces obstacle strength.
Above 700 °C, thermally activated diffusion reduces obstacle strength.
Below 150 MPa, precipitate coarsening or thermally activated diffusion reduces obstacle strength.
Variability in precipitate size distribution produces approximately ±20% uncertainty in the predicted creep-rate reduction.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 50% creep-rate reduction, but the hypothesis is falsified only when the reduction is below 10%. Thus, a 10–49% reduction would contradict the quantified prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
